text:
Kailer Yamamoto hasn't scored in eleven games, and the drought is close to meaningless. He's had 2.8 expected goals in that stretch and 5.69 on the season, which works out to 1.2 per 60 minutes, a rate most top-six wingers would take. Three goals is what a 9.4% shooting percentage gets you; his talent range sits around 14%.

The rest of his game has been excellent. Utah has 63.8% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and his 12 points in 18 games are coming at 2.52 per 60. Evolving-Hockey liked him last season too: 2.0 wins above replacement, 53rd among forwards, with his chances-against impact in the 98th percentile.

The thing to watch is his ice time. He played 11.6 and 15.4 minutes in the last two games after spending most of November between 16 and 20, and he has no shots in either. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says 53% of his shots came off the rush last season, so a line that wins the puck back in the neutral zone suits him best.
